ceiling_directive: Extend the full-observation lower bound and matching finite-sample test uniformly to every fixed assignment probability bounded away from zero and one, with explicit propensity-dependent constants, and document the resulting power through reproducible finite-sample simulations.
improvement_directive: Replace the balanced-assignment-only minimax theorem with a matching full-record root-n result for arbitrary fixed p in a compact subset of (0,1), modifying the four-cell least-favorable construction and likelihood calculation accordingly. Add reproducible simulations showing that the proposed thresholds yield informative size and power at realistic sample sizes.
critique: The note proves observable cross-wave identification, uniform concentration, an exactly unbiased lag-separated statistic, and matching root-n separation bounds, so its sharpness language is supported within the stated experiment. The result is nevertheless confined to iid finite-block innovations, an exact fixed-radius common cylinder rule, two independent no-carryover waves, known exposure propensities, and, for the minimax converse, balanced assignment; the amenable-group extension retains essentially the same rigid block-factor structure rather than covering general observed-network interference. The cross-wave identity itself is a replication-product argument, while the substantive converse is demonstrated through a specialized four-cell submodel, leaving the broader practical importance of the diagnostic insufficiently established. With no application or numerical evidence showing that the conservative bounded-difference thresholds are informative, the package remains a technically worthwhile specialized contribution rather than a field-level econometrics result.
